segments.text: Welcome to the daily Robotics news digest for October 8th, 2026.
Today we cover major updates on humanoid logistics, ROS developments, and the fascinating world of manufacturing automation.
From Humanoids Daily, UBTECH and FAW-Volkswagen expand humanoid robot partnership into factory logistics.
This report details a collaboration focused on developing and testing humanoid robot applications specifically for factory logistics within the automotive manufacturing environment.
The joint plan builds upon prior work where UBTECH robots were utilized for quality inspection at the automaker's Qingdao facility.
The current agreement involves joint development and testing activities aimed at creating demonstration applications and promoting humanoid robot solutions for smart manufacturing.
The partnership seeks to explore the reliability of these robots in performing logistics tasks within the automotive setting.
This development signals a step toward integrating advanced robotics into complex industrial operations.
Further developments in this area will define the trajectory of practical humanoid application in manufacturing settings.
From Planet ROS, ROS Discourse General: Rokoko ROS 2 bridge for Smartgloves II is released.
This announcement details the release of an open-source ROS 2 bridge designed to stream solved hand data from Smartgloves II directly into the ROS 2 framework.

The software provides twenty-six joint hand poses, optional transform information, and visualization of the hand skeleton within RViz, alongside per-hand diagnostics and a calibration service for defining the forward direction.

A single launch command manages the driver, hand solver, and bridge, accommodating either a left or right glove at a time, requiring ROS 2 Lyrical Luth and the Rokoko Device SDK version 0.10.0 or newer.
This development facilitates the integration of advanced haptic data streams into robotic systems.
Further developments in sensory data processing are anticipated across the technology sector.
From NVIDIA Developer Blog, "The Machines that Make the Machines"

, this segment details the development of robotic systems by the NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab and Isaac team to assemble GB300 tester trays through busbar assembly and multi-connector insertion tasks, achieving high success rates by employing a modular pipeline utilizing classical engineering methods, imitation learning, and specialized perception frameworks.

The team developed a new framework named Deep Object Pose Estimation Revisited, or DOPER, to reliably estimate the pose of connectors, demonstrating greater effectiveness than end-to-end learning for tasks involving physical deformation and tight clearances.
The work further highlighted the necessity of robust robotics infrastructure, such as the TALOS system, for the acceleration of real-world deployment of these systems.
This research underscores the integration of classical engineering with advanced learning techniques in physical robotics applications.
Future developments will focus on scaling these modular approaches across complex manufacturing environments.
From Humanoids Daily, "REK Adds Swords to Humanoid Robot Fights With “Deathmatch”".
This report details the addition of swords to the upcoming humanoid robot fighting event hosted by REK in San Francisco on October 9.
The event will feature blade-equipped machines in addition to previous robot confrontations.
The event card includes scheduled fights such as a G1 weapon fight, a T800 bout, and a Rektile versus T-REK match.
The REK CEO stated that swords were incorporated because the robot fights were considered too dangerous.
The event will feature arm-mounted weaponry including Spartan Blades and Claw Blades.
This development signals an expansion of the physical combat elements within the humanoid robot competition.
Further events in this domain are anticipated.
And that's all the circuits for today!
Hope your day is as smoothly programmed as a perfectly executed algorithm.
Until tomorrow, keep building those amazing ideas!
Bye for now.
